Snowflake documents resource monitors that track warehouse credit usage and suspend a warehouse once it hits a credit limit. A hands-on user confirms setting one to stop all warehouses at 20 credits to keep costs from ballooning, and cost anomaly monitors plus notification integrations add alerting on top. Missing for 10: no evidence of idle-time auto-suspend settings for warehouses, no per-query timeout or cancellation of a single runaway query, and no evidence of a budgets feature (anomaly monitors are only in preview).

Snowflake documents Semantic Views as schema-level database objects for declaring business metrics, entities and their relationships once in the database, which covers the core of a governed semantic model. Snowflake documents Snowpipe for continuous ingestion: it loads files in micro-batches as they arrive in a stage, into standard and Iceberg tables. The docs themselves say data becomes available "within minutes", not seconds, and Snowpipe is file/stage-based rather than an API that accepts row-level streaming writes. Missing for 10: a documented row-level streaming ingestion API, evidence of seconds-level query latency, and independent or hands-on corroboration of streaming performance.
